TotalEnergies: a selective, gated AI transformation programme

Full analytical report — revised decision draft, 10 November 2026

Team: Alexandre Waerniers, Vincent Lamy, Yoni Mahieddine, Nahel Bachriri

1. Decision and strategic logic

Proposed resolution [Judgment]: approve a $16.29m gross planning ceiling across Y0 and five operating years for seven initiatives and one shared enabler. Release up to $2.30m at Y0, subject to verified scope, baseline and contractual eligibility. Fund subsequent tranches only against value, adoption, safety and learning gates.

Decision economics [Calculation on assumptions]: central NPV +$3.491m, central IRR 26.4%; probability-weighted NPV +$2.124m and weighted-cash IRR 19.6%, at an assumed 10% common screen. Downside NPV is −$5.370m. No avoided-inaction uplift, H3 commercial receipts or post-Y5 value supports these results.

Mechanism: use the existing Digital Line, Digital Factory and segment platforms to improve measurable operating decisions; business owners and Finance sign the incremental cash. Preserve a bounded H3 experiment in third-party e-SAF technology licensing. The proposal is an external team's hypothesis, not a claim that TotalEnergies lacks AI or already approved these scopes. All project amounts are assumptions unless expressly marked as facts.

2. Company baseline and evidence discipline

Verified facts. TotalEnergies had five operating segments—Exploration & Production, Integrated LNG, Integrated Power, Refining & Chemicals, and Marketing & Services—plus Corporate at year-end 2025. It reported $201.196bn of external sales in FY2025 and 101,513 employees at 31 December 2025 (2025 Universal Registration Document, pp. 6, 49, 474; strategy synthesis, CLM-001). The stated growth pillars are oil and gas, particularly LNG, and Integrated Power. Those facts explain why operating reliability, drilling economics, new energy technologies and customer operations deserve examination; they do not prove the selected proposals are the best investments.

The company already has a Digital Line within OneTech, a Digital Factory, existing segment AI capability, a planned AspenTech industrial-data rollout and a Cognite rollout across operated upstream assets. Its URD says nearly 100 Digital Factory solutions have been developed since 2020 and more than 10,000 AI models are live; it does not disclose equivalent coverage, adoption or cash value per solution (URD, pp. 39, 42–43; AI synthesis; register, CLM-015–019 and CLM-029). The roughly 500-expert Digital Factory figure is disputed across dated sources (CON-001); it is not a staffing baseline for our budget. Existing investments and capabilities are included in each counterfactual, so no case purchases an already-funded group platform again.

The 2025 URD reports a 7.0% post-tax WACC estimate for specified impairment tests (URD, pp. 462, 472; CLM-075). This is a published impairment input, not a published company investment hurdle or branch WACC. The branch and project rates in this report are explicit team assumptions. ROACE is a distinct return-on-capital measure and is never substituted for a hurdle.

Competing evidence. Equinor reported cumulative predictive-maintenance value since 2020, including partners, but its methodology and comparable scope are not established (CLM-036). Shell vendor material describes large deployments without an audited AI-only return (CLM-041). BP's well-planning example gives a speed claim, not an attributable TotalEnergies saving (CLM-068). These examples show feasible use-case classes, not a measured performance gap. The competitor synthesis records the limits. Vincent's Argedis experience is a local observation about French retail delivery and a calibration input for a hypothetical P13 proposal (CLM-074, 078–079); it is neither evidence of group-wide practice nor a statement that this specific project exists or has been funded.

3. Readiness, bottleneck and testable thesis

Using the course's five pillars and five stages (course PDF, session 1; assessment), the outside-in working scores are: business strategy 3/5, technology/data 3/5, AI experience 3.5/5, organisation/culture 2.5/5, and governance 2.5/5. The last two are uncertain because public disclosure does not establish internal adoption, value tracking or model-inventory practice. The provisional group stage is 3, Implementing, potentially approaching 4, Scaling. These are team judgments, not a TotalEnergies internal maturity audit.

The candidate bottleneck is delivery throughput and frontline adoption: subject-matter users may lack protected time to co-build and validate solutions. This is supported by one local Argedis observation and the URD's acknowledgement of organisation/skills adaptation risk; neither proves a binding group-wide constraint. Industrial data availability, value measurement, model governance and talent are serious alternatives. A first cross-segment diagnostic should compare delivery lead time, data blockers, decision ownership, adoption and Finance-signed value on selected workflows. If data access or governance proves the binding constraint, the operating intervention must change. The readiness analysis keeps evidence for and against each candidate and specifies the tests.

Why now [Judgment]. Already-funded data and model capabilities create an opportunity to capture value through use-case-specific workflow changes. Faster deployment would matter only if it creates verifiable incremental cash or a defensible learning option. An unquantified assertion that competitors will overtake the company is not used as a financial benefit or as the cost of inaction.

4. Operating model and change mechanism

The provisional choice is a strong hub-and-spoke, using existing structures rather than a new stand-alone AI organisation. The Digital Line/Digital Factory hub would own common standards, reusable data/model infrastructure, vendor arrangements and a model-and-value register. Segment spokes would select use cases, provide an accountable business owner and own operational change. Finance would establish the baseline, check attribution and sign realised value. HSE, cyber, legal and employee representatives would review relevant uses before deployment. Human experts retain high-impact operating decisions, consistent with TotalEnergies' stated AI principle (CLM-026).

The operating-model comparison assesses a central CoE, hub-and-spoke and federation against size, regulation, talent and maturity. A purely central CoE risks queues and weak business ownership; immediate federation risks duplicated tools and inconsistent controls while common platforms are still rolling out. Federation can be reconsidered for a segment once its data slice, model register, Finance-signed benefits and safety controls pass agreed tests. Actual group decision rights and Digital Factory funding are unknown (CLM-030); the proposal must be reconciled with them before describing an organisational change.

Delivery trio [Assumption to test]. For each approved pilot, pair a hub data scientist, a segment data engineer and a business champion with 20–40% protected time. The latter fraction is a planning assumption, not a current TotalEnergies allocation or an unfunded contribution. A project budget must include or explicitly identify the engineer, manager, frontline training and backfill time. Segment leaders own adoption and the P&L lever; the hub cannot certify its own benefits. Compare this trio with the existing delivery process in the first pilots before scaling it.

Decision Proposed accountable role Control
Pilot selection and business baseline Segment sponsor and Finance Compare the existing process, simple non-AI alternative and incremental AI proposal.
Technical and data design Digital Line / Digital Factory with segment IT Use the smallest necessary data slice and existing contracts first.
Operational release Segment operations lead Human authority, safe workflow, user training and documented adoption.
Financial release Segment sponsor and Finance Recalculate remaining cash flows at the project hurdle; retain sunk and unavoidable cost.
Safety, privacy and regulatory stop HSE, cyber, legal and applicable workforce representatives Block a non-compliant or unsafe deployment irrespective of modelled NPV.

The course's change section asks who changes work, how resistance is handled, what skills are funded and which leading indicators the Comex sees before EBIT appears (course pp. 198–203). For every pilot, record baseline usage, manager participation, exception handling, employee consultation where applicable, operational quality and Finance-verified cash separately. A model used often is not itself a cash saving. The governance draft gives the release structure; named individuals, calendar dates and quantitative thresholds still require agreement.

5. Selected portfolio and capital allocation

Select seven business initiatives plus one shared control enabler. This is a bounded incremental programme, not TotalEnergies' entire AI transformation budget. It reuses established platforms. The four detailed cases are P01, P03, P12 and P13. Geographic and asset eligibility remain G0 conditions.

H1 monetizes existing operations, H2 redesigns adjacent decision workflows, H3 tests a new business model. P03 and P09 qualify as H2 only if the scoped workflow changes planning/operating decisions across teams; a monitoring-only implementation is H1. P12 requires external licensing novelty, not simply a long research cycle. The course's 70/20/10 mix is a heuristic, not an optimization constraint.

6. Four detailed cases

6.1 P01 — Refining predictive maintenance (H1)

Status: Rebuilt working case, 10 November 2026. Economic drivers and unit costs are explicit assumptions, not reported TotalEnergies results. Validate the site perimeter, counterfactual, actual costs and tax before approval. Active calculations: work/finance/portfolio_model_selected.xlsx, independently checked by work/finance/reconcile_selected.py.

1. Decision, problem and existing capability

Proposal: Pilot predictive maintenance on critical rotating equipment at two eligible refining sites, then extend within those sites only when operations and finance confirm value. Asset and site selection are assumptions pending validation. TotalEnergies is already deploying AspenTech's industrial data platform (CLM-018) and has existing maintenance processes; both belong in the counterfactual. This proposal funds an incremental workflow and interventions only where they are not already delivered.

Problem [Hypothesis]: Certain unplanned equipment stops lead to lost margin and avoidable emergency repairs. The number of preventable outages, eligible machines and economic contribution of the sites are unknown. A data platform or an anomaly alert alone does not create value: a verified alert must lead to a safe maintenance action that changes the baseline outcome.

2. Alternatives, horizon and sourcing

Option Decision
Existing scheduled and condition-based maintenance Counterfactual. Compare the proposed system against existing monitoring and documented maintenance activity.
Improved manual thresholds and reliability review Benchmark on the same machines; use this simpler approach if it achieves comparable results at lower cost.
Vendor APM plus site-owned integration and maintenance workflow Working proposal: buy/partner for tools, integrate with existing data and build the site workflow. Contracts and current licenses must be checked.

H1 [Judgment]: Optimises existing refining operations using an established class of maintenance tools. Technology maturity does not prove the local gain. No new enterprise-wide data lake is assumed.

3. Perimeter and benefit drivers

All parameters below are assumptions, not published TotalEnergies site performance. The two sites' actual throughput, ownership share, production constraints and incremental contribution margin must be verified.

Incremental throughput recovery 0.5% Improvement over existing maintenance, not all site outages. Avoid applying it to downtime already excluded from the throughput base.

Full-scale gross benefit = 250,000 × 365 × 0.005 × 0.70 × $6 + $200,000 = $2.11625m/year [Calculation on assumptions]. The scope is two assumed sites, not all group throughput. Equinor's reported $120m since 2020 (SRC-017 / CLM-036) is a cumulative contextual benchmark and does not prove this annual amount.

7. Gates, adoption and risk

  1. Before pilot: site reliability owner, finance and IT establish existing solutions, eligible equipment and production baseline, data rights and the $1.4m spend split. Agree the alert metric, false-alarm tolerance and comparable maintenance baseline before live testing.
  2. Pilot review: reliability engineers validate actionable alerts, safe intervention and actual production/repair economics; finance checks whether incremental throughput was sold. Pause on safety issues; retrain or stop on missed pre-agreed performance thresholds.
  3. Expansion: sponsor releases further spend only if the future incremental case clears the hurdle and the site adoption and security conditions are satisfied. A stop leaves sunk and non-cancellable costs in the programme.

Illustrative financial threshold [Calculation]: with the base costs, tax and ramp unchanged and all benefits scaled together, total five-year NPV at 9.5% reaches zero at approximately $1.080m/year at full scale (51.0% of the modelled $2.116m). This is a full-project sensitivity, not a prospective continuation rule: at the gate, exclude sunk costs and recalculate the remaining cash commitments and attainable benefits. Agree operational reliability and safety thresholds with the site before launch.

The reliability team retains intervention authority; operators and maintenance staff participate in design and receive funded training. Cybersecurity, safety, data completeness and actual licensing scope are gating conditions, not afterthoughts.

  • TotalEnergies 2025 URD: refining throughput CLM-052 and existing data initiatives CLM-018; no claim that the assumed two sites have 250 kb/d.
  • Market ERM is contextual only, CLM-063; the $6/b incremental contribution assumption is not a source-backed TotalEnergies actual.
  • Equinor SRC-017 / CLM-036: $120m cumulative predictive-maintenance value since 2020, including partners; not an annual peer amount or a transferable per-machine return.
  • Discount rate: work/finance/discount_rate_policy.md. Recompute independently in the replacement spreadsheet and validate site baseline, budgets, tax, rates and scenarios before presentation.

6.2 P03 — Deepwater drilling advisory (H2, provisional)

Status: Rebuilt working case, 10 November 2026. The two-rig scope, economic inputs, payment mechanism, costs, tax and ramp are assumptions, not TotalEnergies' observed results. Contracts, eligible assets and incremental benefit require validation. Active calculations: work/finance/portfolio_model_selected.xlsx, independently checked by work/finance/reconcile_selected.py.

1. Proposal and starting point

Proposal: Test a human-supervised planning and drilling advisory workflow across two eligible operated deepwater rigs or campaigns. Identify actual operated assets and obtain agreement from the operator, drilling contractor and relevant partners before committing to a pilot. Existing Cognite deployments and drilling practices remain in the counterfactual (CLM-019); count only incremental capability and cash.

Fact: Mero is operated by Petrobras; TotalEnergies' reported interest was 19.3% in the 2025 announcement (SRC-037, CLM-077). The previous claim that Mero is operated by TotalEnergies was incorrect. This case therefore does not assume the ability to deploy unilaterally at Mero, nor apply the 19.3% figure mechanically to a different contract.

Problem [Hypothesis]: Better use of well and drilling data may reduce non-productive time. A faster operation does not automatically save cash: the contract must permit an earlier rig release, reduce variable charges or create another documented financial benefit. BP's published well-planning example is context, not proof of a TotalEnergies gap or saving (CLM-068).

2. Alternatives, horizon and delivery

Option Assessment
Existing drilling workflow Counterfactual, including existing engineering and contracted tools.
Improved manual or rules-based planning Benchmark using the same wells, staff and contractor terms.
Commercial drilling tools alone Consider existing contract features and compare total costs, data rights and actual incremental gains.
Blended advisory workflow Working proposal: integrate existing data and proven software with company drilling expertise, with no autonomous steering.

H2 [Judgment, provisional]: A cross-functional redesign of the well-planning and operational workflow is proposed. Horizon placement must reflect the selected workflow and adoption cycle, not a desire to rebalance the portfolio. HSE and drilling experts retain operational authority.

3. Scope and incremental benefit formula

Annual assumptions at full scale: two eligible operated rigs/campaigns; six avoidable rig-days per rig per year; $0.400m/day fully avoidable gross spread cost; 80% assumed economic share × 75% payment avoidability = 60% combined realization. These are not verified company figures. Both factors are explicit hypotheses for the same eligible campaigns, not verified contract terms. Do not apply ownership a second time. If the actual economic share is 40%, otherwise unchanged benefit halves to $1.440m/year, below the $1.660m break-even reference.

2 rigs × 6 days/rig/year × $0.400m/day × 60% = $2.880m/year gross incremental cash [Calculation on assumptions]. Verify invoices, full rate composition, actual rig release rights, partner allocation and whether the company already planned the saving. Any time saving without reduced cash payment is reported as capacity or schedule value, not this cash benefit. Avoid overlap with existing procurement savings and the existing savings plan.

4. Costs, data and timing

Amounts $m, nominal; calendar and procurement terms are assumptions. The one-time investment is $1.4m: $0.8m assumed capitalised integration/software ($0.4m Y0 + $0.4m Y1) and $0.6m of one-time integration, commissioning and training expense in Y1. Confirm the accounting treatment and reuse of existing platforms. Recurring software, data engineering, contractor support and run cost are assumed at $0.30m, $0.45m, $0.50m, $0.50m, $0.50m in Y1–Y5.

Assumed benefit ramp: 0%, 30%, 70%, 100%, 100% in Y1–Y5. This assumes a pilot, followed by conditional release, not autonomous operation. The model assumes a 25% cash-tax rate, straight-line depreciation of $0.8m over five years from Y1 and no immediate credit for annual losses; actual jurisdiction, ownership and tax terms must be confirmed. No terminal value or country premium is assumed separately.

Hard dependencies: rights to selected drilling data, contractor integration, operator consent, safely bounded advisory workflow and finance access to invoices. Cognite on operated assets is an existing foundation, not a promise that a specific rig is connected on a chosen date. Well engineering lead and contractor representatives own validation.

6.3 P12 — AI-assisted e-SAF technology licensing option (H3)

Decision: fund a staged experiment in a third-party technology business, reusing the catalyst research concept and its existing cost envelope. Do not approve a production plant or forecast royalty receipts.

Business-model hypothesis: combine AI-assisted catalyst/process discovery with a licensable process package for independent e-fuel developers. The proposed buyer is a third-party plant developer; potential consideration would be development fees, technology royalties and technical support, rather than only margin on fuel produced in company-owned plants. Pricing, addressable buyers, IP ownership and technical differentiation are unknown. No such receipts enter the five-year model.

Existing capability and disconfirmation: TotalEnergies already has CO2 Techno Hub, BioHub and SAF research partnerships. This is not a proposal to create those capabilities again. Infinium describes a third-party technology licensing arrangement in Southeast Asia; that establishes a possible commercial structure, not demand for a competing TotalEnergies package or an achievable return. Before spending, map existing TotalEnergies licensing, partner IP and funded e-fuel research. If this merely improves an internal fuel-production process or duplicates an existing offer, its H3 thesis fails. Stop or reclassify it; do not preserve H3 by relabelling duration.

Why AI: rank candidate formulations and experiments using uncertainty-aware models, then validate with physical tests. Compare against conventional design of experiments using the same laboratory budget. Prediction accuracy alone is not an investment milestone. Blend existing research infrastructure, specialist laboratory partners and commercial/IP expertise. No new foundation model or plant construction is funded.

Costs [Assumptions]: preserve $0.30m CAPEX in Y0, $0.30m CAPEX and $0.40m launch expense in Y1; recurring Y1–Y5 costs are $0.20m/$0.30m/$0.40m/$0.45m/$0.50m. Total gross ceiling is $2.85m. This is a narrow feasibility and laboratory envelope, not funding for certification, a demonstration plant, industrial warranties or commercialization. Existing lab access is a hard condition. The $0.40m launch allowance must cover commercial/IP work and experiment design as well as integration; reprice or stop if it cannot.

Gates [Proposed assumptions]: before Y0, OneTech and Legal establish non-duplication, data and licensing rights. Before Y2, identify at least two qualified third-party developers willing to discuss a defined application and benchmark. Before Y3, require a repeatable result from three independent experimental runs, a pre-registered improvement target against the conventional method, a preliminary freedom-to-operate assessment and at least one documented willingness to enter a paid evaluation (not booked as revenue). The experiment protocol must set the technical improvement threshold before testing. If any commercial or technical condition fails, stop avoidable spending; retain spent cash and a $0.10m closure allowance. No automatic industrial scale-up follows a laboratory pass.

H3 rationale: the proposed transformation is a technology-licensing revenue model serving external developers. The lab work is the means, not the reason for H3 classification. H3 is conditional on this novelty being established at G0. The five-year NPV below measures the cost of exploration only; IRR and payback are inapplicable. No long-term option valuation is asserted.

Sources: TotalEnergies innovation and existing research; Infinium projects, Southeast Asia licensing, accessed 10 November 2026. See the H3 evidence note for scope and limits.

6.4 P13 — French retail demand and controlled markdowns (H1)

Status: Rebuilt working case, 10 November 2026. Project and scenario figures are assumptions unless explicitly identified as facts or local observations; they require financial and operational validation before submission. The active scenario calculations are in work/finance/portfolio_model_selected.xlsx. The decision does not yet authorise deployment.

1. Decision and existing situation

Proposal [Assumption]: Pilot demand forecasting and replenishment assistance with electronic shelf labels and controlled dynamic markdowns in 100 large company-operated French service stations. A successful pilot may justify a separately approved expansion. Expansion beyond the 100-store scope requires a separate investment decision.

Calibration [Assumption]: For this proposed case, Vincent suggests an indicative €1m investment for 100 large French COCO stations, including electronic labels (CLM-078, CLM-079). These are inputs informed by local experience, not evidence of an actual project, company budget or realised result. Scope, contracts and operational baseline require validation.

The programme is presented as a proposed pilot. Before investment, map existing retail capabilities and funded initiatives, so the business case counts only incremental costs and benefits. TotalEnergies' worldwide retail footprint is not used as the pilot denominator (SRC-002 p.13). The comparative baseline retains existing replenishment, pricing, staff and systems.

2. Problem, alternatives and horizon

Problem [Hypothesis]: Store-level volatility creates avoidable perishable losses, out-of-stocks and urgent deliveries; static ordering and pricing may not capture local traffic and seasonality. Actual losses and baseline performance across the 100 stores are unknown.

Alternative Approach Decision rationale
Existing process Current ordering, promotions and local adjustments continue Counterfactual. Measure its actual outcomes; do not assume it is ineffective.
Forecast only Improve orders and stock visibility; no new labels Lower hardware spend may make this preferable. Compare pilot cost and benefits before selection.
Forecast + labels Forecast demand and apply approved markdown recommendations using electronic labels Working base case: combines the proposed pilot's components. Each label/markdown gain must be incremental to forecasting.
Manual rules Improve min/max thresholds and expiry rules without ML Benchmark on the same stores and outcomes; AI is justified only if it adds measurable net value over this option.

H1 rationale [Judgment]: Improve an existing retail workflow for existing customers using established methods. Forecasts and prices remain subject to human control and pricing rules; the first validated benefit is targeted within the pilot, not assumed before it operates.

3. Scope, dependencies and implementation

  • Scope: 100 selected French company-operated stores. Verify stock ownership, price authority, POS coverage and category mix before funding.
  • Hard dependencies: permission to use station/SKU sales and stock history; an eligible POS and label interface; a process for updating shelf prices; data-protection and commercial review. Existing pricing systems and pre-funded label costs are part of the baseline, not repurchased.
  • Soft dependencies: weather and traffic feeds. Begin with a representative pilot if they are unavailable; do not wait for a group-wide data platform.
  • Delivery [Assumption]: a branch retail owner, data engineer and data scientist work with station managers and finance; buy/partner for label hardware, integrate with existing systems, and build or configure the forecasting layer. Contract terms and data rights determine the final sourcing choice.
  • Timeline [Assumption]: Y0 late 2026 decision and setup; Y1 pilot rollout and baseline validation; Y2 expand to the eligible 100 stores after a successful gate; Y3–Y5 operate and measure. These are hypothetical model periods.

5. Benefit drivers and revised financial case

All inputs are assumptions for 100 eligible stores. The central annual benefit is €0.585m: €0.245m waste reduction + €0.200m incremental markdown recovery + €0.140m stock-out recovery. Urgent-delivery savings are excluded until invoices establish avoidable cash. No 2–3 year payback target is used to solve the benefit assumptions.

  • Waste: 100 × €350,000 perishable sales × 70% inventory cost × 4% baseline waste × 25% reduction = €245,000/year.
  • Markdowns: 100 × 1,000 at-risk items × €2 net incremental recovery = €200,000/year. These items must be outside the waste pool. Define SKU/day cohorts and measure net margin after cannibalization, discounts and extra handling. If this cannot be demonstrated, remove the markdown stream.
  • Stock-outs: 100 × €50,000 missed sales × 8% recovery × 35% contribution = €140,000/year. Measure incremental category contribution, not substitution between products.

These equations are transparent planning hypotheses, not observed baselines. A pilot must compare forecasting only, rules-based ordering and forecasting plus labels using matched stores and seasonality. The €1m remains the 100-store rollout ceiling; release only a small instrumented slice before buying all hardware.

7.1 If only half the budget is available

Half of the selected gross envelope is $8.144m. Retain P01, P05, P09, E01 and the initial P12 experiment through Y2, with $0.10m closure/transfer in Y3. This costs $7.460m, leaving $0.684m unallocated. P02, P03 and P13 are deferred in this constrained alternative. No proportional haircut to benefits is used; retained scopes retain their original costs and benefits. P12 receives no automatic continuation beyond the funded experiment.

Scenario NPV at 10%, USD m IRR
Downside -3.367 -20.2%
Base +0.732 17.3%
Upside +2.183 31.5%
Weighted +0.070 10.7%
Severe stress -4.100 -28.0%

The half-budget weighted NPV is only marginally positive. This is a feasible constrained response, not equally attractive performance at half cost. It sacrifices upstream/drilling and retail learning and most of the full portfolio's expected net value. Its remaining headroom is not a forecast saving. The H1/H2/H3 mix remains present, while the H3 commitment is limited to an interpretable experiment. Dependencies and shared governance costs are retained, not halved.

Why the half-budget portfolio is not simply the four featured cases. The featured cases were selected to explain the strategy and its different decision mechanisms, not to fit a 50% spending limit. P01 + P03 + P12 + P13 cost $11.347m; retaining the required E01 controls brings that to $12.287m, or 75.4% of the full envelope, against $8.144m available. Even limiting P12 to Y0–Y2 plus closure gives $11.037m. Keeping all four at half budget would therefore require redesigned asset/store scopes, fixed-versus-variable costs and benefit ramps. Proportional scaling would be misleading. The constrained alternative instead preserves complete, costed operating cases and one bounded H3 experiment. It is a feasible response, not a claim of an optimized subset across all possible scope redesigns.

Full versus constrained portfolio: spending and expected net value on the same five-year basis. All values are calculations on explicit assumptions.

8. Cost of inaction

The baseline includes existing AI, maintenance, trading, retail and research programmes. Doing nothing here means not funding these incremental experiments, not abandoning AI. Potential consequences are slower capture of eligible operating margin, delayed learning and difficulty retaining scarce delivery capability. The magnitude and programme-specific causality are unverified.

Decision treatment: zero additional avoided-erosion cash is booked. The project benefits already compare against continuation; adding the same missed margin as an inaction loss would double count. Talent and customer losses require distinct cohorts, causal effects, economic ownership and incremental prevention costs before any uplift is recognized. A course example or a percentage of group revenue does not validate these inputs. Present the opportunity cost qualitatively and the unadjusted scenarios quantitatively. This meets the inaction discussion without manufacturing a positive downside.

9. Release gates, accountability and adoption

Segment sponsors own operating change; Finance signs baseline and incremental cash; Digital Line/Digital Factory owns reusable technical controls; HSE, cyber and Legal retain veto rights. P01 belongs to refining, P02/P03 to upstream, P09 to LNG, P13 to Marketing & Services, P05/E01 to Corporate and P12 to OneTech with a commercial/IP sponsor. These are proposed roles, not claimed internal appointments.

Gate Metric, threshold and deadline Owner and action
G0 before each Y0 purchase order 100% selected scopes have existing-solution inventory, economic/data rights, vendor/staff cost build and signed comparison protocol Segment sponsor + Finance; no order for an unready scope. P12 also needs a distinct external licensing hypothesis and usable IP.
G1 before Y2 release Zero unresolved critical safety/privacy issues; at least 90% pilot users trained and 60% eligible decisions recorded over the last four weeks, or a workflow-specific threshold agreed before launch Operations + HSE; pause new spend for unsafe or unused workflows. Finance records cash separately from usage.
Cash scale gate before each expansion Positive prospective NPV at the project's hurdle using measured effects and remaining avoidable costs; no duplicate benefit pools Sponsor + Finance; stop or resize on failure. No automatic rollout from a positive original NPV.
P12 before Y3 Technical replication, IP clearance and documented third-party paid-evaluation interest as defined in §6.3 OneTech + Legal + commercial sponsor; stop or reclassify when the external-business thesis fails.
Quarterly portfolio review Actual spending, commitments, cash attribution, adoption, exceptions and cost-to-complete Finance and sponsors; unapproved overruns receive no next tranche. Retain sunk and non-cancellable costs in the forecast.

Monthly business dashboards and quarterly portfolio reviews track the J-curve and leading indicators. Protect 20–40% champion time only where priced into the project staffing plan; managers approve participation and backfill before pilot launch. Staff practice, employee consultation and safe exception handling precede live deployment. Dates are relative to investment approval, not claims of signed internal schedules.

Downside discipline: the model does not assume that general gates magically avoid every loss. H1/H2 downside retains planned spending; P12 explicitly stops with exit cost. Before contracts, obtain cancellation schedules and calculate committed exposure at each gate. Y0 authorisation limits initial purchases, but is not a guarantee of total programme loss. A production plant, new hardware estate or commercial warranty outside these scopes requires a separate approval.

10. Recommendation and defense

Approve the $16.29m gross planning ceiling and release up to $2.30m at Y0 only for G0-ready slices. Subsequent spending is conditional. The central return clears the assumed hurdle, and the weighted case remains positive after paying for H3 exploration and removing unsupported retail delivery cash. The downside is negative; the proposal relies on measured continuation decisions, not a claim of risk-free investment.

The core thesis is to improve value capture in selected workflows using existing capabilities, with an explicit experiment in external technology licensing. This is a bounded programme within TotalEnergies, not proof of a group-wide maturity deficit. The reduced-budget response sacrifices meaningful value and learning; it is an alternative if capital is constrained, not the recommended default.
